Position.description:
A point in the venue's local metric frame, in metres.

Never latitude/longitude. Lat/lon exists only at the circuit pack's origin and at the device's location adapter (plan.md section 10).

PositionFix.description:
A resolved position, with the honesty attached.

`accuracy_m` is a one-sigma radius, and `residual_m` is what the solve could not explain. They fail apart on purpose: a tight `accuracy_m` beside a large `residual_m` means the anchor map is wrong, not that the phone is confused, and that is the difference between recalibrating a venue and blaming a handset.

accuracy_m.description: positional one-sigma. Feeds Confidence; never zero.

anchors_used.description: anchors that contributed. Zero for GNSS, and a two-anchor fix is a weighted centroid rather than a trilateration — the count is how a reader tells which.

heading_deg.description: degrees clockwise from north. Null when speed is below the noise floor, because the heading of a stationary phone is noise with a number on it.

residual_m.description: RMS of the range residuals, metres. Null when the source does not solve (GNSS).

speed_ms.description: metres per second, from successive fixes. Null until there are two.

PositionSource.description:
Which radio produced a position.

Not decorative and not merely diagnostic: accuracy differs by an order of magnitude between these, the confidence model weights on it, and an operator reading a sparse zone is entitled to know whether the dots there are GNSS fixes in the open or BLE fixes under a stand.
